t: No part of any money appropriated herein or included under any contract authority herein granted shall be expended for the payment of any commission on any land purchase contract in excess of 2 per centum of the purchase price.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the word "commission" signals an advisory body, but here it means a broker's fee on land purchases. The section is purely an appropriations spending limitation capping that fee at 2 percent. It provides no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: payment of any commission on any land purchase contract in excess of 2 per centum of the purchase price

qwen_block.w: This section imposes a financial limit on commissions paid for land purchase contracts. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. It is a budgetary restriction, not a participation mechanism.
qwen_block.s: No part of any money appropriated herein or included under any contract authority herein granted shall be expended for the payment of any commission on any land purchase contract in excess of 2 per centum of the purchase price.

opus.w: This section only limits spending: appropriated funds can't pay a commission above 2 percent of the purchase price on a land purchase contract. "Commission" means a sales fee, not an advisory commission, and the land contract is a transaction, not a consultation. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to sue.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "commission" or "land purchase contract" points to an outside body or party. It fails because "commission" here means a broker's fee, not a body of people, and the contract is just a purchase transaction. The section only caps how appropriated money can be spent, and no outside party has a say in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a financial limit on commissions for land purchase contracts. It does not require the federal government to consult or coordinate with any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. It is a restriction on expenditure, not a mechanism for public participation.
qwen_chat.s: No part of any money appropriated herein or included under any contract authority herein granted shall be expended for the payment of any commission on any land purchase contract in excess of 2 per centum of the purchase price.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that limiting commissions on land purchases involves contractors or outside parties, thus implying some form of interaction. However, this is merely a financial restriction on how appropriated funds can be spent. It does not require the government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from any outside party (such as states, tribes, the public, or experts) before making a decision. It is a budgetary constraint, not a participatory process.
